packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - BLIND IMAGE READING (unverified)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of these leaves. This is a blind first reading. Beyond the rules I listed the packet directory once (ls, to learn the file names and pixel sizes; packet.json was not opened). Nothing else was opened.

Packet contents: 4 faces. Each has one reduced overview plus six native-resolution tiles (2 columns x 3 rows, overlapping):
  Face A: overview image-001; tiles 002-007
  Face B: overview image-008; tiles 009-014
  Face C: overview image-015; tiles 016-021
  Face D: overview image-022; tiles 023-028

Conventions: line numbers count text lines from the top of the named image, ignoring partial lines cut by the tile edge at the very top (I note these where relevant). Where tiles overlap, I transcribe each physical line once, under the tile where I read it, and give the overlap. Expansions are in (), uncertain readings end with (?), unread text is [illegible]. Tironian et (7-shaped) is given as "et". Initials and capital strokes touched in red are marked [red X]. Expansions are tentative throughout. The hand is a small, compressed, heavily abbreviated Gothic book hand, so many suspensions are my guesses.

=====================================================================
FACE A (overview image-001; tiles 002 TL, 003 TR, 004 ML, 005 MR, 006 BL, 007 BR)
=====================================================================
Layout survey (observation): verso-type face with the ruler on the left and the gutter on the right. Two columns of about 38 lines each. No running title is visible. At the top centre of the upper margin there is faint red/brown writing ("[illegible] ha(?)"), too faint to read. Rubrication: a large red I at about col. a line 9 and a large red D (two lines high) at about col. b line 6. Small initials stroked in red throughout, often at authority names (Beda, Aug(ustinus), Gregorius, Jeronimus, Seneca(?)). In col. a, the first two lines and lines 5-8 are in a lighter red-brown ink, possibly rubricated or retouched text, possibly just a lighter ink load. Col. b lines 3-4 have red pen strokes running into the right margin. Small marginal ticks/letters in the right margin of col. b. Pale stain at col. b lines 26-27, with the ink partly blotted there.
Tentative interpretation: a florilegium or moral compilation built from short sententiae introduced by authority names. Not a text with commentary: I see no glosses, no lemma/commentary layout and no underlining.

Face A limitations: col. a lines 1-22 and col. b lines 1-16 have many [illegible] spots. The ink is lighter or blurred there, and several lines in col. a seem to be retouched in red-brown. Expansion of the authority abbreviations is tentative. Selected and read: most of both columns, with the clearest stretches at 004.24-006.17 (Beati quorum ... / Loth ... sodomam / carnal pleasures) and 003.17-007.14 (rota / diuites / superbia / periculosior est res prospera).

=====================================================================
FACE B (overview image-008; tiles 009 TL, 010 TR, 011 ML, 012 MR, 013 BL, 014 BR)
=====================================================================
Layout survey: recto-type face with the ruler on the right. Modern pencil foliation "(10)-2" in the top right corner. Two columns, col. a about 39 lines, col. b about 39 lines. A strip of the facing page with marginalia shows at the far left edge of the overview; I did not read it. Rubrication: a red M (two lines high) at col. a line 7, after a red horizontal line that fills the end of line 6 (end of a section). A large red I at col. b line 30 begins a section headed "Incipit admonicio ..." (see below). In col. a an ink blot stands on an initial at line 19. "Questio" markers abbreviated "Q(uestio)" with a red-touched Q recur through both columns. Col. b line 1 has two tall flourished long-s/f signs in the ascender space, perhaps marking a correction or decoration; I am unsure which. Lines 1-2 of col. a are in a lighter red-brown ink like Face A.
Tentative interpretation: a run of questions and answers (Questio ... Aug(ustinus) ...) with a new item beginning "Incipit admonicio".
